detail: Science Corp. raised $400 million in Series D funding to advance its brain-computer interface platform.
why_relevant: As a prominent BCI developer, Science Corp. offers direct alignment with neural engineering and brain-computer interface research.

detail: WearOptimo raised A$7.75 million in funding to advance the development and commercialization of its AI-powered microwearable sensors for continuous physiological monitoring.
why_relevant: WearOptimo's AI-driven microwearable platform directly intersects biosignal processing, continuous sensor hardware, and machine learning.

detail: Paradromics partnered with NVIDIA to advance AI computing infrastructure for brain-computer interfaces.
why_relevant: Paradromics is building high-data-rate neural interfaces, offering top-tier experience in machine learning applied to high-density neural signals.

detail: Cambridge NeuroWorks launched to accelerate the translation of novel neurotechnology research into practical clinical applications.
why_relevant: Focusing on neurotech translation provides relevant insight into translational neuroscience and clinical neural device development.

detail: NextWave TMS expanded its depression treatment options through the deployment of accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation.
why_relevant: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is a core non-invasive neuromodulation modality relevant to BME students interested in brain stimulation therapies.

detail: ROOK partnered with Burn Boot Camp to streamline the integration of wearable health sensor data.
why_relevant: ROOK's focus on aggregating wearable biosignal data aligns well with biosignal processing and data engineering skill sets.

detail: MiniMed is expanding its product line with its first upcoming insulin patch pump and continuous diabetes devices.
why_relevant: Wearable drug-delivery patch pumps represent key medical device engineering applications combining embedded sensors and closed-loop algorithms.
